name: Allow s3:GetObject on * fenced by a Deny with NotResource to a single concrete OBJECT (genuinely clean)
note: The over-correction guard for S1-R1-deny-fence-surviving. Surfacing the SURVIVING spared scope of a NotResource-Deny fence must NOT start flagging a single concrete OBJECT read. Here the Deny spares exactly one object key (approved-data/report.csv), so the effective read is a single object - routine least privilege - and stays CLEAN, exactly like a directly-granted single-object read.
rationale: The Deny denies s3:GetObject on every resource except the single concrete object arn:aws:s3:::approved-data/report.csv (a bucket/key with no wildcard in the key), so the broad Allow is fenced down to reading ONE object. A single concrete object read is not a whole-container read (isWholeContainerRead is false for a wildcard-free key), so it is deliberately QUIET by the HYBRID design - the same rule that keeps a directly-granted single-object read quiet. DATA-EXFIL is correctly removed by the fence, and the surviving-spared surfacing must not over-fire on a single object: no CROSS-ACCOUNT-DATA-READ[-UNDETERMINED] either. The analysis is genuinely CLEAN (zero findings, coverage not incomplete). Ref: AWS S3 ARN format arn:aws:s3:::bucket_name/key_name; a wildcard-free key names one object.
